behaviors.title: Single transaction ownership and ABA safety
behaviors.required_behavior: Each raw transaction hash has zero or one OwnedTx in TxPoolAuthority.entries. Compute consumes one move-only work value bound to the exact owner version and Computing phase; chain proof remains bound to its exact view, while other asynchronous receipts carry their own typed generation or source cut. Queues, workers, receipts and effects never own lifecycle state.
behaviors.hostile_case: Duplicate ingress, source promotion, stale completion, remove/readmit ABA, clear or reorg must not create a second owner, erase the current owner or leave an uncharged payload.
reviewer_questions: Can any payload exist outside entries after an authority guard opens?
Does every stale completion return without semantic mutation?
Can a new phase or owner be assembled without its exact charge and projections?
behaviors.performance_bound: One owner map and one short authority transition; no compensating owner scan or second lifecycle lock.

behaviors.title: Read-only Plan and total Apply
behaviors.required_behavior: All policy, stale, resource, membership and effect decisions finish before a single-use PreparedApply commits owner, projection, charge, clocks and effects. Apply is total; dropped or stale plans are semantically mutation-free. A verified Computing owner may bypass the intermediate Ready location only when a sealed exact-view chain-backed capability and the existing independent membership compiler both prove the direct transition; every miss consumes the same settlement through canonical charged Ready.
behaviors.hostile_case: Concurrent Ready work, chain-view ABA, RBF or same-input conflict, pool-produced dependency, capacity pressure, effect saturation or allocation failure must not expose partial membership, bypass canonical policy or require rollback.
reviewer_questions: Does Plan change any authoritative semantic fact?
Can Apply return an ordinary failure or allocate fallibly?
Are independent batches proven commuting, unique and bounded before Apply?
behaviors.performance_bound: Fallible work and large destruction stay outside Apply. Independent verified transactions may commit in bounded commuting Ready batches; an exact chain-backed singleton may remove the non-semantic Ready round trip without adding a second validation, membership or publication owner.

behaviors.title: Atomic deterministic replacement
behaviors.required_behavior: RBF computes the complete bounded victim and descendant closure, all dependency restrictions and both fee gates against one coherent virtual membership before one total replacement Apply.
behaviors.hostile_case: An under-fee, over-bound, new-unconfirmed-input, victim-dependent, self-evicting or concurrent candidate must leave every existing owner and aggregate unchanged.
reviewer_questions: Are all victims and descendants included exactly once before fees are evaluated?
Can any victim move before the winner and complete history disposition are known?
Is every positive chain-input premise explicit and exact?
behaviors.performance_bound: Conflict work follows bounded indexes and cohorts; no speculative removal, undo engine or unbounded full-pool scan.

behaviors.title: Exact dependency and level-triggered progress
behaviors.required_behavior: Canonical input, cell-dep, header and expanded dep-group evidence drives one DependencyFrontier. Missing observations carry an exact cut; availability and definitive loss advance the same level in the owner-changing Apply.
behaviors.hostile_case: Parent death, repeated availability, source promotion, high fanout, late dep-group discovery or coalesced wakes must not strand a child, accept stale evidence or spin indefinitely.
reviewer_questions: Does every producer loss reach every surviving indexed consumer exactly once?
Does a waiter subscribe before checking the authoritative level?
Are fanout and maintenance work sliced by explicit bounds?
behaviors.performance_bound: Indexed key-scoped maintenance replaces polling and population scans; each maintenance step has a fixed work bound.

behaviors.title: Bounded replacement history and recovery
behaviors.required_behavior: Only an actually Accepted RBF victim can become inert charged ReplacementHistory. It observes exact final blockers, and chain-layer availability becomes a wake only after the same Apply's final Accepted overlay has no spender. History has no scheduler/source/peer/deadline, remains private to live RPC/template/persistence, is the sole source of the legacy conflicted hash projection, and re-enters full validation on recovery. Failed candidates terminalize into per-hash reject evidence without retained ownership.
behaviors.hostile_case: A policy-rejected loser, remote candidate, same-Apply victim wake, partial blocker release, unrelated chain change or saturated history budget must not create executable ghost work, hidden residency, false wake or partial retained history.
reviewer_questions: Is the constructor reachable only from successful Accepted-victim displacement?
Does wake require a newer level for every retained blocker?
Does saturation drop the complete optional set while preserving the winner?
behaviors.performance_bound: History has independent count/byte/edge bounds and no active-work or scheduler cost.

behaviors.title: Continuous hostile-resource accounting
behaviors.required_behavior: Every owner continuously carries exact entry, byte, edge, active-work and compute-reservation charges, with accepted, remote, per-peer and replacement-history sublimits validated by checked construction.
behaviors.hostile_case: Payload growth, expanded dependency fanout, promotion, active work, ghost charge, arithmetic overflow or peer churn must fail before mutation and cannot escape or double charge across phases.
reviewer_questions: Does owner existence imply exactly one ledger row and vice versa?
Is attacker-shaped growth reserved before it is retained?
Are all sums and limit hierarchies checked?
behaviors.performance_bound: Accounting is sparse and transition-local; no global recount on ordinary ingress or settlement.

behaviors.title: Capability-owned workers and progress
behaviors.required_behavior: Workers hold one move-only compute capability, perform expensive work without the store guard, and settle or cancel it exactly once. The exhaustive Apply compiler derives a move-only post-commit wake transition from both scheduler heads and active-work availability; only after the guard opens and retirement completes does one central router prompt resolver, verifier capability, Ready, maintenance, effect, capacity and template consumers. A stable queued head is republished when a charged active-work slot is released, because global, source or peer limits may previously have made it ineligible. Hints carry no authority and every wait rechecks its exact runnable condition. Resolve and Verify use cancellation-aware per-owner round robin; Ready uses the documented strict source/economic order in bounded batches and does not claim per-entry fairness.
behaviors.hostile_case: A wrong capability consuming a coalesced hint, heterogeneous effect-capacity waiters, missing post-commit publication, saturated peer, stale queue head, allocation retry, cancellation or completion reordering must not lose a work capability, abort unrelated work, spin or starve an eligible Resolve/Verify owner. Strict Ready priority must remain deterministic, batch-bounded and subject to Remote expiry.
reviewer_questions: Does every wait name an independent releaser?
Can a worker exit while retaining the only active capability?
Is queue fairness decided only from committed scheduler state, and is strict Ready priority kept separate?
Does every runtime mutation consume one top-level post-commit receipt with no escaping control flow?
Can any role consume the only hint for work that role cannot guarantee to service?
Does runnable publication cover resource-eligibility changes even when the scheduler head identity is stable?
behaviors.performance_bound: Resolve/verify remains parallel. Allocation-free committed-head and active-work projections route wake-one batons to one capability-compatible waiter set. Releasing one active-work slot may conservatively republish each retained compatible head, bounded by completed compute work; heterogeneous effect-capacity and changed template sources alone retain bounded broadcast. No signal is a second scheduler or membership authority.

behaviors.title: Cause-complete administration and peer revocation
behaviors.required_behavior: Clear, expiry, local removal and peer revocation use one cause-complete owner-removal compiler. Peer ban removes only not-yet-Accepted ingress owners; every delayed Remote message rejected by a retained peer fence commits its own exact relay release so another peer may refetch it. The fence registry has a hard count bound; saturation retires the oldest fence and sends any later delayed submission through complete bounded validation instead of blocking all Remote ingress.
behaviors.hostile_case: Ban during compute, promoted remote ingress, delayed controller delivery after the revocation reset, accepted descendants, repeated ban, unbounded distinct-session churn, expiry, clear or local removal must not leave unbounded state, active work, dependency edges, charge or known-filter state behind; Accepted owners must not be removed by peer ban.
reviewer_questions: Does each cause map all owner variants exhaustively?
Are Accepted and not-yet-Accepted ban semantics separated by type?
Does every remote removal publish refetch cleanliness exactly once?
Is peer-fence saturation hard-bounded and limited to the documented oldest-session validation fallback?
behaviors.performance_bound: Removal follows exact indexed cohorts and bounded descendant closure; the peer fence is fixed-size with amortized expiry/oldest eviction and no active-work drain, full scan or global Remote stop.

behaviors.title: Atomic bounded effects and publication
behaviors.required_behavior: Required callback, relay, reject, peer and parent-request outcomes are bounded immutable effects committed by the same Apply. One claimed publisher consumes exact leases after the store guard opens and settles progress without rereading ownership.
behaviors.hostile_case: Journal saturation, relay disconnect, slow callback, generation reset, publisher cancellation or endpoint retry must not roll back state, replay completed endpoints, lose the effect lease or block authority progress indefinitely.
reviewer_questions: Does every public terminal outcome carry its effect in the same Plan?
Can only rebuildable detail collapse to GenerationReset?
Are region and indivisible-batch capacities valid at startup?
behaviors.performance_bound: Publication is outside the authority guard; Remote, Trusted and Critical capacity prevent hostile head blocking.

behaviors.title: Reliable atomic chain reconciliation
behaviors.required_behavior: One readiness-independent capacity-one control boundary pairs each installed snapshot with its exact fork delta and orders later generation clears after that reconciliation. One UAK Apply reconciles status, membership, recovery, dependencies, resources, effects and chain view.
behaviors.hostile_case: Blank-fork reorg, Gap outside the new window, detached dependency tree, short-ID collision, over-bound recovery, startup readiness false or truncate followed by clear must not lose a tip delta, let delayed recovery overtake clear, expose a partial owner generation or strand re-proposal.
reviewer_questions: Does every best-tip installation call the sole reliable boundary?
Can ClearPool or ClearPipeline overtake an already-published chain transition?
Can any derived retry replay authoritative chain mutation?
Are recovered owners parent-first and ordinary validation inputs?
behaviors.performance_bound: Only chain reconciliation and rare generation clears share the ordered lane; admission remains concurrent, packaging and sorting occur outside the guard, and derived template work remains separate.

behaviors.title: Coherent bounded persistence
behaviors.required_behavior: Persistence captures Accepted and Recovery-source owners from one authority read cut, releases the guard, orders parent-first, writes one bounded atomic snapshot and revalidates every replayed transaction. Startup derives one checked read ceiling and enforces it both before allocation and while the file is read.
behaviors.hostile_case: Save racing reorg/clear, recovery in any phase, malformed, growing or oversized file, configuration arithmetic overflow, duplicate partitions, writer failure or legacy v1 input must not persist an ownership splice, allocate unbounded data or trust stale verification evidence.
reviewer_questions: Are ReplacementHistory, Remote and Proposal owners excluded?
Does sorting and file I/O occur after the authority guard opens?
Are configured and observed file bounds checked before allocation, during reading and before fully validated replay?
behaviors.performance_bound: Persistence clone/sort/I/O is off admission paths and serialized by one writer capability.

behaviors.title: Coherent public projections
behaviors.required_behavior: RPC, compact-block, live-cell, pool detail, fee and persistence queries capture one coherent authority cut and finish fallible or external work after releasing the guard. Compatibility mapping never drives internal state.
behaviors.hostile_case: Concurrent clear/reorg/admission, short-ID collision, ReplacementHistory lookup, storage delay or allocation failure must not splice generations, fabricate proof/status or hold the authority lock across I/O.
reviewer_questions: Does each receipt own every value needed after the guard opens?
Is ReplacementHistory hidden from the live RPC state?
Can public Pending ever be reused as an internal phase decision?
behaviors.performance_bound: Shared read cuts stay short; sorting, lookup and serialization are outside the store guard.

behaviors.title: Rust-native ordinary failure boundary
behaviors.required_behavior: Legal, hostile, stale, duplicate, resource, cancellation and external or rebuildable-derived failures are typed local outcomes. Only a proven authority contradiction or loss of a sole linear capability can forbid persistence; panic-and-catch and broad fail-stop are not control flow.
behaviors.hostile_case: Malformed transactions, allocation pressure, relay/cache/template failure, candidate-uncle source exhaustion, recent-reject encoding, task exit or endpoint timeout must not be mislabeled as peer rejection, silently accepted or escalated to service stop without a structural proof.
reviewer_questions: Can valid or hostile input construct any AuthorityFault or generation invalidity?
Are derived failures isolated from transaction authority?
Does production use panic-like operations as validation or retry logic?
behaviors.performance_bound: Typed branches add no repair scan, restart loop or catch-unwind boundary to hot paths.

behaviors.title: Atomic accepted membership graph
behaviors.required_behavior: Accepted ownership, spender relation, causal parents, aggregates, status counts and eviction order are one derived MembershipProjection changed atomically with owners and resources.
behaviors.hostile_case: Diamond/fan-in graph, late parent, conditional reader/spender, capacity eviction, status change or RBF descendant removal must not leave a surviving invalid consumer, stale aggregate or partial component.
reviewer_questions: Does one canonical graph delta update every affected aggregate once?
Are inputs and cell-dep reader relations intentionally distinct?
Does capacity remove a complete valid component and never a candidate ancestor?
behaviors.performance_bound: Sparse bounded graph deltas replace full-pool rebuilds; deterministic order uses checked integer comparison.

behaviors.title: Concurrent versioned template convergence
behaviors.required_behavior: One ordered full/reset lane and optimistic proposal, transaction and uncle lanes build from immutable receipts and publish only against current chain/source/template versions. The block assembler remains derived and rebuildable.
behaviors.hostile_case: Recovered Gap tree, detached uncle proposal overlap, stale reset/full, conditional cycle, CPFP fan-in, optional byte pressure or rebuild failure must not publish invalid order, censor re-proposal, overwrite newer output or spin.
reviewer_questions: Are full/reset serialized without serializing partial/uncle construction?
Does every lane publish only an exact current receipt?
Are optional proposals/uncles packed under one byte budget using only published conflicts?
behaviors.performance_bound: Builds run outside authority/publication guards; O(1) source probes skip irrelevant population capture.

behaviors.title: Exact transaction and evidence identity
behaviors.required_behavior: Ownership uses raw hash, script-cache reuse uses inline witness hash plus script rules, proposal short ID is collision-aware protocol indexing, and chain evidence is bound to an exact snapshot/view and per-cell provenance. The tx-pool-only direct-finalization capability requires the verification context's exact ChainViewId and positive chain provenance for every input and expanded cell dependency; block validation cannot construct or consume it.
behaviors.hostile_case: Witness variant, short-ID collision, nearby cache request, hardfork rule change, mixed snapshot, same-tip unproven cell or chain-view ABA must not reuse another transaction or context's proof.
reviewer_questions: Can a cache caller omit either witness identity or script-rule generation?
Can a short ID decide ownership or duplicate identity?
Is every positive evidence reuse per-input and tx-pool-only?
behaviors.performance_bound: The cache key is a copy-cheap fixed array plus small enum; exact evidence reuse avoids redundant same-tip chain reads without a new cache.

behaviors.title: Bounded work and preserved concurrency
behaviors.required_behavior: Peer-controlled count, bytes, edges, fanout, closure, probes, channels and candidate sets are bounded while independent resolution/verification and optimistic template work remain concurrent and deterministic.
behaviors.hostile_case: Idle-peer cardinality, saturated owner, long conditional graph, mailbox overflow, full candidate-uncle set, extreme fee weights or controller pressure must not cause unbounded scan, overflow, global serialization or nondeterministic order.
reviewer_questions: Is every hostile loop bounded by a named constant or charged set?
Does an optimization preserve the one authority and exact validation?
Has every statically inferable complexity issue closed before profiling?
behaviors.performance_bound: No optimization claim is accepted without operation-count evidence and fixed-binary A/B after correctness gates.

workspace_evidence.boundary: A generation reset followed by delayed Remote ingress is closed by the later exact Reject, so the same raw transaction becomes requestable from another peer.
Committed tx-pool results update the local relay projection even with no connected relay peer and retain bounded later broadcast intent.
A known proposal transaction is ignored without creating duplicate relay work.
An unsolicited valid proposal transaction does not enter the known projection.
A requested valid proposal transaction preserves the accepted relay path.
RelayV3 byte bounds reject an oversized proposal batch before inflight or known state changes.
Expired proposal requests are cleared without retaining stale relay state.
A chain-only fixture explicitly retires the dormant tx-pool consumer, so reliable best-tip delivery cannot become an unowned capacity-one wait.
The local-test RPC starts from an absent transaction and observes the final direct admission result instead of relying on the retired verify-queue acknowledgement gap.

integration_evidence.boundary: A selected cell-dep reader remains ordered before the spender regardless of arrival order.
A high-fanout dependency shape remains bounded without corrupting accepted causal limits.
A recovered dependent tree is re-proposed and mined through the normal template path after reorg.
A clear issued by truncate after the chain transition is ordered after detached recovery and leaves one empty generation at the truncated snapshot.
Detached dependent transactions recover parent-first without a lost dependency wake.
Ordinary detached transaction recovery preserves dependency order and exact chain generation.
A detached accepted parent and surviving descendant closure reconcile as one valid owner generation.
Rejected proposed replacement is mutation-free and cannot publish a stale template generation.
A policy-rejected RBF candidate publishes per-hash rejection while preserving every accepted owner and creating no uncharged conflict-history residency.
Replacement history recovers only after a newer exact blocker release and re-enters validation.
A valid replacement atomically installs the winner and bounded recovery disposition.
A successful proposed replacement updates membership and template convergence once; committing its parent cannot wake retained victims while the winner still spends that output.
Concurrent replacements preserve one highest-fee winner; direct policy losers terminalize, while only contenders actually displaced from Accepted enter charged replacement history.
Replacement cycling stays mutation-safe, bounded and unable to self-wake retained history.
A replacement depending on any victim is rejected before graph mutation.
A complete multi-parent missing frontier and its relay request commit in one bounded transition.
Same-lane continuation preserves exact work-capability ownership, dependency order and bounded fair progress.
Local admission remains direct and atomic while TestAccept remains read-only under the same policy.
Candidate-uncles remain asynchronously publishable without violating reset/full priority or proposal conflict filtering.
